entities.summary: Thomas of Frignano (1305–1381) was an Italian Franciscan theologian who became Minister General of the Order of Friars Minor and was approved by Pope Gregory XI as patriarch of Grado. He played a crucial role in the development of Franciscan theology and was instrumental in shaping the Order's spiritual direction. Through his leadership, Thomas of Frignano helped establish the Order as a major force in medieval European religious life. His commitment to the Franciscan ideals of poverty, simplicity, and compassion had a lasting impact on the Order and its followers. The exact date of his birth is unknown, but his death in 1381 marked the end of an era for the Order of Friars Minor. Thomas of Frignano's legacy continues to be felt in the modern Franciscan world, where his emphasis on spiritual growth, community, and social justice remains a guiding principle. As the leader of the Order, he oversaw a period of significant growth and expansion, which led to the establishment of new houses and the spread of Franciscan spirituality throughout Europe. His influence can still be seen in the many institutions and organizations that bear the name of the Order, from the University of Florence to the Friars Minor's charitable work around the world. Through his writings and teachings, Thomas of Frignano helped to shape the intellectual and spiritual landscape of medieval Europe, leaving behind a rich legacy that continues to inspire and motivate people to this day.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Thomas of Frignano played a crucial role in shaping the spiritual direction of the Order of Friars Minor and contributing to its growth and expansion during his leadership. His commitment to the Franciscan ideals of poverty, simplicity, and compassion had a lasting impact on the Order and its followers.
